newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Refinery in troubled Nigerian oil city shut - paper.
newsitem.headline: Refinery in troubled Nigerian oil city shut - paper.

text.p: An oil refinery in Nigeria's midwestern city of Warri has been shut following ethnic clashes recently which rocked the city, Oil Minister Dan Etete was quoted as saying on Saturday.

The semi-official Daily Times said Etete disclosed this when military leaders met him on Thursday at the refinery to discuss the clashes which swept Warri in response to the relocation of local council headquarters.
The minister said the refinery, which supplies western Nigeria, had to be closed when its storage tanks became full and vessels were unable to sail into Warri to load oil products.
Warri refinery has the capacity to process 125,000 barrels of crude daily into oil products.
Etete said a fuel shortage could hit western Nigeria, including Lagos, if the facility was not reopened soon, and he requested the military to secure the waterways to allow ships to sail in.
The navy and troops were deployed in the Warri area about two weeks ago to stop the fighting, between armed youths of the rival Ijaw and Itsekiri tribes.

Scores of people were killed and fire swept several villages in the clashes, which erupted when the military government moved the capital of Warri south local government to an Itsekiri settlement from an Ijaw town.

Nigeria has three other refineries. These plus the Warri plant have a combined notional capacity of 445,000 barrels per day, although they normally operate well below that level because of technical and other problems.
The crisis also forced Royal Dutch Shell Group's Nigerian unit to shut some of its oil facilities.
